unmapped_findings: EDS-measured chemical composition of the 17Al alloy (at.%, Table 1): Fe 43.2, Mn 34.8, Al 17.0, Cu 5.0; nominal Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) (b0013, b0017).

The 17Al alloy in the solution-treated (solid-solution) state is a single α (BCC) phase with a coarse grain structure (Fig. 3b), and its solution-treated hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV is higher than that of the 15Al alloy because the hardness of the solution-treated alloys increased with rising Al content, attributed to solid-solution strengthening (b0036).

For high-Al Fe-Mn-Al-based alloys, precipitation of the D0₃ phase after solution treatment and quenching is common, and the increase in Al content increases the amount/size of D0₃; however, the D0₃ phase was not observed in the alloys with maximum hardness, suggesting its depletion accompanied β-Mn precipitation and growth (b0065).
